verdict.rationale: Pulumi documents infrastructure definition in TypeScript, Python, Go, .NET, Java and more, using standard language features like loops, functions and classes. Community users confirm TypeScript's type system and standard dev tooling work for infra. One user notes that resource outputs are futures and can't be used directly in conditionals, which limits but does not contradict the capability. Missing for 10: explicit first-party documentation of IDE support (autocomplete/type checking in editors), which is only implied by community mentions of standard dev tools.

support.subject: As a developer, I can define infrastructure in a general-purpose programming language with types, loops, and IDE support

citations.quote: Pulumi supports TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, .NET, Java, YAML, and HCL.
use standard language features like loops, functions, classes, and package management that you already know and love
managing infra plus k8s resources with TypeScript's type system is really nice
You can write libraries with secure defaults and use standard dev tools to audit and refactor.
